answer: Each agent receives a signing key, but the economy grants influence only after a scarce, nontransferable stake has remained locked through a challenge period. A trellis of peer attestations links each key to a history of completed trades; disputes can slash the stake and erase that history. An oasis or lagoon may offer privacy, but neither lets a new key inherit reputation. To multiply identities, an attacker must lock fresh capital per key and risk losing it, making Sybil influence costly rather than free.
